messages.author: 4be88a5fc86a040f
messages.subject: Re: using bootstrap components in a shinyUI(pageWithSidebar app - ?
parts:
If I understood your question right, you don't need an external component to display your data in a window with scrollbar. If the data is vector as in example, you simply place it as a text with <br> tags at the end of each line, inside a div of a fixed height and overflow set to "auto" to enable scrollbar. Like this:

ui.R
library(shiny)
shinyUI(pageWithSidebar( 
  headerPanel(""), 
  sidebarPanel(
     div(id = "textContainer", style = "height:100px; overflow:auto", htmlOutput('htmlData'))  
  ),
  mainPanel(
  )
))

server.R
library(shiny)
data <- 1:30
shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  output$htmlData <- renderText(paste0(data, "<br>", collapse = ""))
})

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: using bootstrap components in a shinyUI(pageWithSidebar app - ?
parts:
If you can mix and match them using HTML + JavaScript, then you should be able to mix and match them using shinyUI as well. In the particular case of our pageWithSidebar and gridster, since each of those has a pretty strong opinion about what the overall layout of the page is like, you might have trouble there. But for other things like Google Charts, JustGage, d3, etc. the components generally play nice on the same page.

One key thing to remember is that everything inside of the shinyUI call, is merely a producer of HTML. Take any sub-expression of shinyUI and print it at the console and you'll see what it does. If you have two components that don't work together, try printing (or use cat(as.character(...)) for nicer looking output) each of them out and see if you can figure out why they are not compatible.
